findings.claim: The Verification Status Rules table and the normative jq rule in the same file disagree on packages with a non-critical `unverified` claim: the table's `verified` row requires "no claim is `blocked` or `unverified`", but the jq (and both reimplementations in check-research-package.sh) only demote for critical non-`verified` claims or any `blocked` claim, deriving `verified` anyway.
findings.evidence: Table: "`verified` | every critical claim is `verified`, no claim is `blocked` or `unverified`, ..."; jq in the same hunk: `elif ([critical[] | select(.label != "verified")] | length) > 0 or ([claimset[] | select(.label == "blocked")] | length) > 0 ... then "partial" else "verified" end`. A claim set with all critical claims `verified` plus one non-critical `unverified` claim matches no table row (the `partial` row also omits this case), yet the drift check — which "recomputes it and fails when the declared value differs" — derives `verified`. A synthesizer following the table cannot pick any status the checker will accept.
findings.suggested_fix: Align the two statements: either add `or ([claimset[] | select(.label == "unverified")] | length) > 0` to the jq/checker `partial` branch, or change the table's `verified` row to "no claim is `blocked` and no critical claim is `unverified`".

findings.claim: A clean full-scale run self-blocks at stage 10: report.md frontmatter is written at stage 09 (when the derivation can yield at most `partial`, since `integrations.adversarial_review_used` is still false for scale=="full"), the only post-review mutation is `lower_report_status` (verified→partial, never raises), but export derives the manifest's `verification_status` from the post-review checkpoint — so a run with a passing Feynman gate and a PASS review yields manifest `verified` vs report `partial`, and check-research-package.sh's report↔manifest agreement check fails validate_stage 10.
findings.evidence: run-research.sh: `lower_report_status` only rewrites `verification_status: verified` → `partial`; stage 10 runs `review_report` then `export-package.sh` then `validate_stage 10` → `check-research-package.sh --package` → block 10 on failure. check-research-package.sh python block: `report.md verification_status=... but manifest ...` → FAIL on mismatch. okf-research-format.md derivation: `verified` requires `($c.scale == "full" and ($c.integrations.adversarial_review_used | not))` to be false, i.e. is unreachable at stage-09 write time for full runs. No scenario in driver-contract.sh exercises this because fixtures/stage-runner.sh stage 09 hardcodes `feynman_grade: null` / `verification_status: partial`, keeping every fixture derived at `partial`.
findings.suggested_fix: After a non-BLOCK review (or inside export-package.sh), rewrite report.md `verification_status` to the value derived from the final checkpoint before validate_stage 10 runs, and add a driver-contract scenario where the gates pass (feynman_grade 0.8, misconceptions_absent 1.0, judge PASS) asserting the run completes with `verified`.

findings.claim: The goals extraction for the research target swallows all failure (`python3 ... > "$WORK/goals.md" 2>/dev/null <<'PY' || true`): if python3 errors, the redirection still creates an empty goals.md, the packet builds with an empty `goals` field, and the judge silently loses the query and sub-questions it needs to assess coverage.
findings.evidence: The hunk `python3 - "$PACKAGE" > "$WORK/goals.md" 2>/dev/null <<'PY' || true` followed by the packet comment "Goals of the run ... This is what 'coverage' is judged against." The change's own constraint states: "Every script touched keeps set -euo pipefail semantics and non-zero exit on failure; no silent `|| true` on a gate."
findings.suggested_fix: Fail closed (exit 2) when the goals extraction fails, or record an explicit `goals_error` field in the packet so the judge knows coverage cannot be assessed.

findings.claim: The `lower_report_status` path is never exercised: the fixture stage 09 always writes `verification_status: partial`, so the review-critical assertion "report frontmatter lowered to partial" and the review-unavailable/review-without-verify `partial` assertions all pass even if the lowering code in run-research.sh is deleted outright.
findings.evidence:
fixtures/stage-runner.sh stage 09: `printf -- '---
...
verification_status: partial
...'` unconditionally; driver-contract.sh review-critical asserts `test "$(report_status)" = "partial"` — true before the review ever runs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a fixture knob (e.g. FIXTURE_REPORT_STATUS=verified) so at least one scenario writes `verified` at stage 09 and asserts it is lowered to `partial` by a CRITICAL verdict, a refused review, or an unavailable judge.

findings.claim: A recorded review refusal or judge-unavailable block is terminal: on resume the driver will re-run and repair stage 05, but the idempotency guard `(.review != null) or (.blocked_review != null)` skips re-judging forever, so a transiently-refused package can never reach `verified` even after the verification artifact is restored.
findings.evidence: run-research.sh `review_report`: `if jq -e '(.review != null) or (.blocked_review != null)' "$CP"; then log "report review already recorded; not re-judging"; return 0; fi`, combined with the derivation clause `(($c.blocked_review // null) != null)` → `partial`; driver-contract.sh review-without-verify enshrines "resume does not re-judge a recorded review".
findings.suggested_fix: Allow re-judging when `blocked_review` is set and `validate_stage 05` now passes (clear `blocked_review` on successful re-review), or document the permanence explicitly in SKILL.md's verifier-before-reviewer rule.

findings.claim: The `SLUG="${PACKAGE_ID%-[0-9]...}"` recomputation immediately after package resolution is dead code — it is neither exported nor referenced anywhere else in the driver (write-provenance.sh computes its own SLUG).
findings.evidence: run-research.sh hunk: `SLUG="${PACKAGE_ID%-[0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9][0-9]-[0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f][0-9a-f]}"` appears once, directly above the `export RESEARCH_PACKAGE_ID=...` line, with no later use of `$SLUG`.
findings.suggested_fix: Delete the line, or export it if stage runners are meant to consume it.
